cyclin D1 is not associated with metastatic potential, whereas Ki‐67 is associated with metastatic thin melanomas, and that both cyclin D1‐ and Ki‐67‐positive melanomas have a significantly worse prognosis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of cyclin D is not associated with melanoma progression, while Ki‐67 may be a useful prognostic biomarker for melanoma patients with thin melanomas.
the cyclin D1 expression in thin melanoma is not a prognostic factor.
cyclin D1 expression is a strong prognostic factor for metastatic thin melanoma, but Ki‐67 expression is not.
The main takeaway from our work is that

cyclin D1 expression is significantly higher in metastatic thin melanomas compared with non‐metastases and that cyclin D and Ki‐67 co‐expression is significantly associated with metastatic thin melanoma.
cyclin D1 is an excellent biomarker of melanoma metastasis and Ki‐67 is a biomarker of melanomas that are likely to progress to metastatic disease.
Ki‐67 and cyclin D1 are independent predictors of metastasis, but only in the context of other clinical parameters.
